transcript: I am a wimp, and I just saw what many are calling the scariest play on Broadway, Paranormal Activity, which is based on the movie series of the same name. Although this is an original story. and I'm happy to say that I survived, but I am pretty sufficiently spooked. The show follows an American couple who just moved into a new house in London, and spooky things start happening. That is all I will say without spoiling anything. I actually enjoyed the show a lot more than I thought I would. It is a wild ride and really keeps you on your toes. You never really know when the next scare is gonna happen, which can be quite tense. I was very nervous for a majority of this play. I think that this play is really effective in getting you to not trust anything that you are seeing, to the point where you're like, oh, my god, there's something behind that door, or there's something in that shadowy corner. You'll, like, swear you see a shadow moving in the background. And that is in many ways the scariest thing about this play. The fear of the unknown and what could be lurking around the corner. I do think that a lot of the physical scares in the show are very well executed. I have heard that the show has some sightline issues if you are on the sides of the theatre. I was in the middle section, so I can't really speak to that, but that's definitely something to be aware of. But the effects are really well done, on par with anything in Harry Potter and the Cursed Child or Stranger Things. Now, as someone who sees a lot of theatre, sees a lot of magic specifically, I did find some of the illusions to be a bit telegraphed, but just judging by the reactions around me, there seem to be a lot of genuine surprise. And even if you do know what's going to happen, these moments are still pretty effective. Now, I do have some qualms with the actual script itself and the story. There are character motivations that aren't always super clear and plot lines that get brought up but are seemingly never resolved. There are also these very long blackout transitions between scenes, and I do get that there's probably no other way to Do these transitions. But they did take me out of the show every single time, and they were pretty long. But even with those negatives, I do think that the show is very effective at what it sets out to do, which is to tell a spooky ghost story on stage in the theatrical medium. And it does that really well. If you like horror, I do think that you will enjoy this. And if you, like me, don't enjoy horror, I do think you'll be able to handle it. But know, when people say it's spooky, they're not lying. Paranormal Activity is going to be a Broadway Ben recommendation.
